fields.questionText: Chord AB of a circle with centre O and radius 21 mm subtends an angle of 120° at the centre. Find the perimeter of the minor segment formed by chord AB (the region bounded by chord AB and the minor arc AB). (Use √3 = 1.73 and π = 22/7)
fields.answer: Perimeter of minor segment = (44 + 21√3) mm ≈ 80.33 mm
solutionSteps: Draw OC ⊥ AB. Then C is the mid-point of AB and ∠AOC = ½ × 120° = 60°.
In right △OCA: sin 60° = AC/OA ⇒ √3/2 = AC/21 ⇒ AC = 21√3/2 mm, so AB = 2AC = 21√3 mm.
Length of minor arc AB = (120/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 21 = 44 mm.
Perimeter of minor segment = arc AB + chord AB = 44 + 21√3 = 44 + 21 × 1.73 = 44 + 36.33 = 80.33 mm.

rationale: Restored √3, 60°, fractions; 'shaded region' made explicit as minor segment (answer confirms arc+chord); retagged to Areas Related to Circles (120° segment is within limit).

fields.subtopic: Area of Sector and Perimeter of Segment
fields.questionText: A chord of a circle of radius 14 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find the area of the smaller sector and the perimeter of the smaller segment. (Use π = 22/7)
fields.answer: Area of smaller sector = 308/3 cm² ≈ 102.67 cm²; perimeter of smaller segment = 86/3 cm ≈ 28.67 cm
solutionSteps: OA = OB = 14 cm and ∠AOB = 60°, so △OAB is equilateral ⇒ chord AB = 14 cm.
Area of smaller sector = (60/360) × (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 308/3 cm² ≈ 102.67 cm².
Length of minor arc AB = (60/360) × 2 × (22/7) × 14 = 44/3 cm.
Perimeter of smaller segment = AB + arc AB = 14 + 44/3 = 86/3 cm ≈ 28.67 cm.
fields.finalAnswer: Area of sector = 308/3 cm² (≈ 102.67 cm²); perimeter of segment = 86/3 cm (≈ 28.67 cm)

rationale: Restored ° in stem, fractions and cm² units; values unchanged (308/3, 86/3); retagged to Areas Related to Circles (60° within limit).

fields.questionText: A quadrilateral PQRS circumscribes a circle, touching the sides PQ, QR, RS and SP at A, B, C and D respectively. Then PA + CS is equal to:
solutionSteps: Tangents from an external point are equal: PA = PD (from P) and CS = SD (from S).
PA + CS = PD + DS = PS. Correct option: (c) PS.

fields.questionText: O is the centre of a circle. AB and AC are tangents drawn to the circle from an external point A, touching it at B and C. If ∠BAC = 65°, then find the measure of ∠BOC.
solutionSteps: ∠OBA = ∠OCA = 90° (tangent ⊥ radius at point of contact).
In quadrilateral ABOC: ∠BAC + ∠BOC = 360° − 90° − 90° = 180° ⇒ ∠BOC = 180° − 65° = 115°.

rationale: Restored ∠ and °; stem self-contained without figure; clean 2-step solution.

Perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord ⇒ AP = PB.
In right △AOP: AP² = OA² − OP² = 5² − 3² = 16 ⇒ AP = 4 cm, so AB = 2AP = 8 cm.

fields.questionText:
PQ is a diameter of a circle with centre O. R is a point on the circle at which a tangent is drawn. A line through O parallel to PR meets this tangent at S. Show that SQ is a tangent to the circle.
OR
A circle has centre O. Tangents drawn at points A and C of the circle intersect at B. If OA ⊥ OC, show that quadrilateral OABC is a square.
solutionSteps: [Variant 1] OR ⊥ RS (tangent ⊥ radius). OP = OR ⇒ ∠OPR = ∠ORP. Since OS ∥ PR: ∠ROS = ∠ORP (alternate angles) and ∠QOS = ∠OPR (corresponding angles) ⇒ ∠ROS = ∠QOS.
In △ORS and △OQS: OR = OQ (radii), ∠ROS = ∠QOS, OS common ⇒ △ORS ≅ △OQS (SAS) ⇒ ∠OQS = ∠ORS = 90°.
OQ ⊥ SQ at Q, which lies on the circle ⇒ SQ is a tangent at Q.
[Variant 2] ∠OAB = ∠OCB = 90° (tangent ⊥ radius) and ∠AOC = 90° (given) ⇒ ∠ABC = 360° − 270° = 90°, so OABC is a rectangle.
OA = OC (radii) — adjacent sides of the rectangle are equal (also BA = BC, tangents from B) ⇒ OABC is a square.
fields.strategyHint: Use tangent ⊥ radius and congruence (SAS) for Variant 1; for Variant 2 show all angles 90° and adjacent sides equal.

rationale: Both variants are fully describable in words; removed figure references; corrected faulty angle-equality reasoning in variant 1 proof.

fields.questionText: TP and TQ are tangents from an external point T to a circle with centre O. If ∠PTQ = 70°, then ∠POQ =
fields.explanation: ∠OPT = ∠OQT = 90° (tangent ⊥ radius). In quadrilateral OPTQ, ∠POQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 70° = 110°. Therefore, the correct answer is 110°.
solutionSteps: ∠OPT = ∠OQT = 90°; in quadrilateral OPTQ, ∠POQ = 360° − 180° − 70° = 110°.

rationale: Self-contained without figure; removed figure reference, tightened explanation.

fields.questionText: PA and PB are tangents from an external point P to a circle with centre O. If ∠APB = 50°, then ∠OAB =
fields.explanation: ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°, so in quadrilateral OAPB, ∠AOB = 360° − 180° − 50° = 130°. △OAB is isosceles (OA = OB), so ∠OAB = (180° − 130°)/2 = 25°. Therefore, the correct answer is 25°.
solutionSteps: △OAB is isosceles (OA = OB = radius).

rationale: Defined centre O and external point in text; figure not needed; clarified reasoning.

fields.questionText: XY and X'Y' are two parallel tangents to a circle with centre O, touching it at P and Q respectively. Another tangent AB, with point of contact C, intersects XY at A and X'Y' at B. Prove that ∠AOB = 90°.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] Join OP, OC, OQ. Since XY ∥ X'Y' and OP ⊥ XY, OQ ⊥ X'Y', P, O, Q are collinear (PQ is a diameter). In △OPA and △OCA: OP = OC (radii), OA common, PA = CA (tangents from A) ⇒ △OPA ≅ △OCA (SSS).
[1 mark] Hence ∠POA = ∠COA; similarly △OQB ≅ △OCB ⇒ ∠QOB = ∠COB.
[1 mark] ∠POA + ∠COA + ∠COB + ∠QOB = 180° (POQ is a straight line) ⇒ 2∠COA + 2∠COB = 180° ⇒ ∠AOB = ∠COA + ∠COB = 90°.

rationale: Named contact points P, Q in text (figure not needed); removed junk construction text; mark-prefixed steps sum to 3.

fields.questionText: Two circles touch each other externally at A. QR is a common tangent to the two circles, touching them at Q and R respectively. The common tangent at A meets QR at P. If AP = 4.2 cm, then the length of QR is:
solutionSteps: Tangents from P: PQ = PA = 4.2 cm and PR = PA = 4.2 cm.
QR = PQ + PR = 8.4 cm. Correct option: (c) 8.4 cm.

rationale: Setup fully describable in text; removed figure reference; added working.

fields.questionText: PB is a tangent at B to a circle with centre O. AB is a chord of the circle of length 24 cm and at a distance of 5 cm from the centre. If the length PB of the tangent is 20 cm, find the length of OP.
solutionSteps: Let OM ⊥ AB, OM = 5 cm. The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord ⇒ MB = 12 cm.
In right △OMB: OB = √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 cm (radius).
PB is tangent ⇒ PB ⊥ OB. In right △OBP: OP = √(13² + 20²) = √(169 + 400) = √569 cm.

rationale: Stem self-contained; removed figure reference and garbled marking residue; restored squares.
Two-circle configuration (points P, A, S, positions of M,N,T) needs the figure; scheme itself notes ambiguity of TB (45 vs 56 cm).

fields.questionText: From an external point P, a line is drawn which cuts a circle with centre O at A and B (A lying between P and B). OC is drawn perpendicular to the chord AB, meeting it at C. Prove that PA · PB = PC² − AC².
fields.answer: PA · PB = (PC − AC)(PC + CB) = (PC − AC)(PC + AC) = PC² − AC²
solutionSteps: OC ⊥ AB ⇒ C is the mid-point of AB (perpendicular from centre bisects the chord) ⇒ AC = CB.
PA = PC − AC and PB = PC + CB = PC + AC ⇒ PA · PB = (PC − AC)(PC + AC) = PC² − AC².

rationale: Restored '−' and squares; described secant PAB in words (the tangent PT was irrelevant to the proof); proof fully self-contained.
Position of A and Q (and that A, O, Q are collinear, which the proof relies on) is fixed only by the figure; not stated in text.
A true via distance formula: OA = 2, (x−2)² + 4 = 4 ⇒ x = 2; R false (centre is not mid-point of every chord). Content is Coordinate Geometry; retagged.

fields.questionText:
A circular fountain in a park has centre O and radius 5 m. A lamp post stands at point P, 13 m from O. Two straight paths PA and PB run from the lamp post and just touch the fountain's boundary at A and B.
(i) Find the length of path PA. [1]
(ii) What is the measure of ∠OAP? Give a reason. [1]
(iii) Find the area of the quadrilateral OAPB enclosed by the two paths and the radii OA and OB. [2]
fields.answer: (i) PA = 12 m (ii) ∠OAP = 90°, since the tangent at a point is perpendicular to the radius through it (iii) 60 m²
fields.explanation: PA is a tangent, so OA ⊥ PA and PA = √(OP² − OA²) = √(169 − 25) = 12 m. PA = PB (tangents from an external point), so △OAP ≅ △OBP and area OAPB = 2 × ½ × 5 × 12 = 60 m².
solutionSteps: (ii) ∠OAP = 90°, because the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. [1]
(iii) PA = PB = 12 m and OA = OB, so △OAP ≅ △OBP; area △OAP = ½ × OA × PA = ½ × 5 × 12 = 30 m². [1]
Area of OAPB = 2 × 30 = 60 m². [1]
fields.strategyHint: Tangent ⊥ radius gives a right triangle; tangents from one external point are equal.

rationale: Authored row used Class 9 chord-distance content with only 2 parts; rebuilt as an in-syllabus tangent case (i)(ii)(iii) 1+1+2 = 4 marks, solved.
Number of common tangents of two circles is outside 2026-27 Circles (tangent at a point, two tangent theorems); also mis-tagged 3-mark MCQ. No natural in-limit repair without replacing the question.
